sub_questions.question: Is there a way to test what my knowledge base will retrieve before plugging it into a live app?

claims.claim: The Hit Testing panel is found on the dataset (opened from the dataset).
claims.guide_evidence: the Hit Testing / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page

claims.claim: You type a sample query and it shows exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores.
claims.guide_evidence: lets a builder type a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores

claims.claim: Hit Testing works without needing to run the full app.
claims.guide_evidence: without needing to run the full app

claims.claim: Hit Testing is useful for checking chunking and indexing choices before wiring the dataset into a retrieval node.
claims.guide_evidence: Before publishing an app that uses a dataset, the Hit Testing / retrieval-test panel

evaluation.rationale: The guide fully backs the answer. It sends Yuki to the Hit Testing panel on the dataset page, which shows the chunks a query would retrieve and their similarity scores without running the full app. The remark that this helps sanity-check chunking and indexing follows reasonably from the guide, and nothing needed to go to a human.
